html:
Homi Bhabha was the physicist who built India's nuclear programme. He founded its two main research centres and planned its reactors.

He was born in 1909 into a rich Parsi family of Bombay, related to the Tatas (see the Parsis). Sent to Cambridge to become an engineer, he turned to physics and did well. The scattering of electrons by positrons is named after him, and in 1937 he helped explain how cosmic rays make showers of particles in the air.

He was on holiday in India in 1939 when the war began and could not go back. He worked for a time under C. V. Raman in Bangalore. In 1944 he wrote to the Tata trust asking for money for a school of physics, and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research opened in Bombay the next year.

After independence Nehru gave him a free hand. He chaired the Atomic Energy Commission from 1948. Asia's first research reactor outside the Soviet Union started at Trombay in 1956. He drew up a three-stage plan to make power from India's large stocks of thorium, and he said openly that India could build a bomb if it chose.

He died in 1966 when an Air India plane hit Mont Blanc. India tested a device in 1974 (see Smiling Buddha).
sum: Homi Bhabha was the physicist who built India's nuclear programme. He founded its two main research centres and planned its reactors.
